title: Torn from behind
hookLine: the shirt is torn from the back, and a witness says that proves who ran

cards: He runs for the door. Yusuf has said I seek refuge in Allah, and now he does the most practical thing a person can do with temptation. She runs after him.
They both race for it, the Qur'an says, and she catches hold of his shirt from behind, and it tears. Then the door opens, and there, standing in the doorway, is her husband. Everyone freezes.
It's a moment straight out of a courtroom drama, except there's no courtroom and no lawyer. Just two stories, one husband, and a torn shirt.

teach.b: Surah Yusuf. She speaks first, fast: what's the penalty for someone who meant harm to your wife, except prison or a painful punishment? She doesn't even say what he did; she jumps to the sentence.
Yusuf answers simply: she tried to turn me from myself. That's all. Then a witness from her own family speaks.
The Qur'an says only a witness of her household; who it was, the text doesn't say. Some commentators report it was a wise man of her family; others tell a story that it was an infant who spoke.
The witness says: look at the shirt. If it's torn from the front, she's telling the truth and he's lying. If it's torn from the back, she's lying and he's telling the truth.
It's almost a detective's rule. Someone lunging at you tears the front. Someone running from you gets caught from behind.
The husband looks. Torn from behind. He says: this is your scheming.
To Yusuf: leave this alone. And to his wife: ask forgiveness for your wrong. Notice what Yusuf did not do.
No speech. No attack on her.
He said one true sentence and let the evidence speak.

teach.h: A WITNESS: LOOK AT THE SHIRT.
teach.b: And this is the second shirt in the surah. The first came home with false blood on it, and it lied.

teach.h: THE SECOND SHIRT TELLS THE TRUTH.
teach.b: This one is torn from behind, and it tells the truth.
There's one more shirt still to come in this story. Keep an eye on the shirts.

how: Muslims often point to the torn shirt as an example of Allah bringing the truth to light, and to Yusuf's calm answer as the way to respond when falsely accused.

o: a cloak worn by travelers in a caravan
a robe of honor given by a king
shirt: the one whose tear showed who ran

games.q: who did what in the story — tap the pairs.
p: she tried to turn me from myself

s: Yusuf defended himself with a long speech
he said one sentence: she tried to turn me from myself.
the witness came from the wife's own family
the Qur'an says a witness of her household. who exactly, it doesn't say.
a shirt torn from behind meant he had attacked her
torn from behind meant he was running away, and she caught him.

games.q: you're the witness from her family. two stories, one husband, a torn shirt. how do you settle it?
o: ask the servants who they believe.
look at the shirt: torn in front or behind?
trust the lady of the house.
games.why: if the shirt is torn in front, she's truthful; if behind, he is. it was torn from behind.

practice: Think of a situation where you feel misunderstood, or accused, or where someone has the story wrong, and notice how much you want to explain, defend, send the long message, win.

Now imagine saying one true, calm sentence and stopping there, letting the facts, the shirt, do the rest, and say it to yourself a few times. If you pray, you can ask for the truth to come out in its own time.

wordCard.voice: Qamis, shirt: the one torn from behind, that showed who ran and who chased, and let Yusuf stop after one true sentence.

orig.note: Arabic: shirt — a word that carries Surah Yusuf from one turn to the next.

carryVoice: Your line: the shirt tells. One true sentence was all Yusuf needed. See you on day sixty-two.
